chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

When a woman is menstruating, salat (prayer) is not permissible for her, and she must perform wudu (ablution) of the salat (prayer) at the time of every salat (prayer), then sit in a pure place and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, glorify Him, declare His oneness, and praise Him for the measure of her salat (prayer), then attend to her need.

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: when she becomes pure, there is no qada' upon her for anything she left of the salat (prayer), but qada' is upon her for what she left of the sawm (fasting).

key_terms.تَذْكُرَ: to engage in dhikr, remembrance of Allah
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up an omitted obligatory act after its time has passed
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: ritual wudu (ablution) performed at prayer time

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman have to make up missed prayers and fasts in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a menstruating woman: salat (prayer) is not valid for her during menstruation, yet she is instructed to maintain devotional remembrance of Allah at the times of prayer. It also clarifies that after becoming pure she does not make up missed prayers, but she must make up the fasts missed during that period.
